  "text": "The public library called to say my overdue book was ready to be returned.

“I don't have a library card,” I said.

“We know. Your mother checked it out for you.”

My mother had died before I learned to read.

The librarian gave me an address and asked me to come before sunset.

I found the building between two shops I'd passed every day for years. Both shops were closed. The library wasn't.

Inside, a woman in a green cardigan slid a picture book across the desk.

“This isn't mine.”

“Look at the last page.”

The illustrations showed a little boy eating breakfast, tying his shoes, standing beside a hospital bed.

On the last page, my mother sat beneath a tree. There was room beside her on the bench.

Her painted face turned toward me.

The librarian placed a pen in my hand.

“Just sign here.”

“What happens if I do?”

“You return what you borrowed.”

I looked at the checkout slip.

Under TITLE, someone had written TWENTY-SEVEN MORE YEARS.

Under BORROWER was my mother's signature.

Outside, the shops switched on their lights.

In the picture, my mother stood. She was shaking her head.

The librarian tightened her grip around my wrist.

“She understood the terms.”

My mother pressed both painted hands against the page.

I pulled away. The pen left a long blue scratch across the desk.

Behind me, the door clicked shut.

The librarian sighed and reached beneath the counter.

“All right,” she said. “We'll contact the guarantor.”

She set a second book before me.

On its cover, my daughter was learning to walk."
